title: Sea Harrier FA2

sources.title: DCS AV-8B Night Attack Harrier Manual CH 1-15 (Harrier principle)
JoyPro cockpit catalog (panels, items and grip functions of the variant)

intro: The Sea Harrier FA2 is the Royal Navy's carrier fighter version of the Harrier, a jet that can take off and land straight up because its Pegasus engine blows through four swivelling nozzles. The pilot sits high under a bubble canopy with a centre stick; his left hand works the throttle and the nozzle lever beside it. The FA2 adds the Blue Vixen radar and AMRAAM missiles. Its radar switches on the grips are not documented in the sources used, so the radar designator is listed in a general form.

areas.name: Head-up display
areas.text: The HUD in front of the pilot.

panels.name: HUD
panels.text: The head-up display with the symbols of the weapon aiming computer.
panels.context: The pilot reads flight data and missile cues here while looking outside.

controls.name: Head-up display
controls.text: The glass screen in front of the pilot's eyes that shows flight numbers and aiming marks (head-up display). It shows flight data, the radar target and the missile launch cues, so the pilot can read them while looking outside.
controls.context: The pilot keeps his eyes on it during take-off, landing and every attack, instead of looking down at the instruments.

controls.name: HUD controls
controls.text: Knobs that set the brightness of the HUD and how many symbols it shows (declutter).
controls.context: The pilot turns down the brightness at night and removes symbols he does not need.

panels.name: Radar display (Blue Vixen)
panels.text: A head-down screen for the Blue Vixen radar, which can find aircraft flying low against the sea (look-down), track several at once and guide AMRAAM missiles.
panels.context: The Blue Vixen and the AMRAAM made the FA2 a real long-range fighter.

controls.name: Multifunction head-down display
controls.text: The screen that shows the radar picture, the tracks of the aircraft found and the weapon status.
controls.context: The pilot picks targets on it with the radar designator on the throttle.

controls.name: Display bezel keys
controls.text: Buttons around the edges of the screens. Each one picks the word printed next to it on the screen, so the same button does different things on different pages.
controls.context: With them the pilot changes the radar mode and the display format.

areas.name: Stick, throttle and nozzle lever
areas.text: The grips and levers the pilot holds.

panels.name: Control stick
panels.text: The centre stick with the trim switch, the weapon release button and the trigger.
panels.context: In the hover the stick also works the reaction controls, small air jets at the nose, tail and wing tips that steer the aircraft when the wings give no lift.

controls.name: Control stick
controls.text: The stick the pilot holds in his right hand. Pushing it forward lowers the nose, pulling it back raises the nose, and moving it left or right rolls the aircraft to that side. When hovering, the same movements open the reaction control jets.
controls.context: It is the main flight control; on most bindings it is the joystick's X and Y axes.

controls.name: Trim switch
controls.text: A small switch on top of the grip for the trim, small adjustments so the aircraft flies straight without the pilot holding the stick. Forward trims the nose down, back trims it up, left and right trim the roll.
controls.context: The pilot trims after every change of speed or configuration, so the stick feels light again.

controls.name: Weapon release button
controls.text: A button on top of the grip under the thumb. Pressing it releases or launches the missile or the bombs.
controls.context: The pilot chooses the weapon first on the armament panel; this button then sends it on its way.

controls.name: Trigger
controls.text: The trigger at the front of the grip, under the index finger. Pulling it fires the Aden gun pods under the fuselage.
controls.context: It only fires when the weapons are armed with the master arm switch; the HUD or sight shows where the shots will go.

panels.name: Throttle and nozzle lever
panels.text: The throttle, the nozzle lever beside it, the STO stop and the switches on the throttle grip.
panels.context: The left hand moves between throttle and nozzle lever; the STO stop presets the nozzle angle.

controls.name: Throttle
controls.text: The lever that makes the Pegasus engine stronger or weaker, like a car's gas pedal. Forward gives more thrust, back less. The Pegasus has no afterburner.
controls.context: The pilot sets it for take-off, climb, cruise and landing; on most bindings it is the throttle axis of the HOTAS.

controls.name: Nozzle lever
controls.text: A smaller lever beside the throttle that turns the engine's four nozzles. Fully forward points them back for normal flight; pulled back it points them down to hover, and further to the braking stop to push the aircraft backwards.
controls.context: This lever is what makes the Harrier special: the left hand moves between throttle and nozzle lever for take-off, hover and landing.

controls.name: Short take-off (STO) stop
controls.text: An adjustable stop on the nozzle quadrant. The pilot sets it to the nozzle angle he wants for a short take-off, so the nozzle lever can be pulled back quickly to exactly that angle.
controls.context: In a short take-off the aircraft rolls fast, then the pilot snaps the nozzles to the STO stop and it lifts off.

controls.name: Transmit button
controls.text: While this button is held, the radio sends the pilot's voice; when it is released, the radio listens again.
controls.context: It works like the button of a walkie-talkie; the pilot uses it to talk to the tower and to other aircraft.

controls.name: Airbrake switch
controls.text: This switch opens and closes the airbrakes, panels that open into the wind to slow the aircraft down.
controls.context: The pilot opens them to lose speed quickly, for example before landing or to avoid flying past a target, and closes them to speed up again.

controls.name: Water injection switch

positions.name: ON
positions.text: Water injection on: more hover thrust.

controls.text: This switch sprays water into the engine. The water cools it, so it can give more thrust for a short time.
controls.context: The pilot uses it for hovering and vertical landing on hot days or when heavy.

controls.name: Radar target designator
controls.text: A tiny thumb joystick on the throttle grip that moves the radar cursor left and right and in range. Pressing it locks the target under the cursor. Its exact place among the FA2's radar switches is not documented.
controls.context: The pilot uses it to pick targets on the radar or sensor picture without taking his hand off the throttle.
